findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the wrong provider
findings.body: The method is documented to return the BouncyCastle security provider, but the implementation returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`. On a standard JVM this is the SUN (or SUNJSSE) provider, not BouncyCastle. Any caller that relies on this method to obtain BouncyCastle (e.g. to register it with `Security.addProvider` or to pass it to JCA factories) will get a different provider and silently produce wrong crypto results (e.g. signature verification failures, or worse, signatures produced with a non-BC provider being treated as BC). Since this is the only implementation in the new `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` that is supposed to work without the full Keycloak crypto stack, it must either return a real BouncyCastleProvider (or null/throw if BC is not available), not the default-keystore provider.

findings.title: Dead code in concatenatedRSToASN1DER wastes allocations
findings.body: In `concatenatedRSToASN1DER`, the two calls `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` create new ASN1Encoder instances, write integers into their internal ByteArrayOutputStreams, and then discard the results without ever calling `toByteArray()`. They have no effect on the returned value. The call sites inside `writeDerSeq(...)` already create fresh encoders for the same integers. These two lines are pure dead code that allocate two extra ByteArrayOutputStreams per signature conversion. They should be removed.

findings.title: Test constructor declares throws Exception and does shared setup
findings.body: `ECDSAAlgorithmTest` generates the EC KeyPair in its constructor and declares `throws Exception`. JUnit 4 test class constructors should not throw checked exceptions; setup that can throw must be done in a `@Before`/`@BeforeClass` method. With the current code, if `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC")` ever fails (e.g. on a JVM without EC support, or under a restricted security policy), the JUnit runner will report the failure as a framework error rather than as a test failure, and the per-instance key pair means a key generated by a previous test run is never reused even when that would be desirable. Move the KeyPair generation into a `@Before` method (or a `@BeforeClass` static field) and let the test methods just do the work.

findings.title: Dynamic string passed as format string to logger.debugf
findings.body: The new code builds a `StringBuilder` containing the ignored providers and then calls `logger.debugf(builder.toString())`. JBoss Logger's `debugf(String, Object...)` treats the first argument as a printf-style format string. If any provider class name (or anything concatenated into the builder) ever contained a `%` character, the call would throw `IllegalFormatException` instead of logging the message, and the entire `init()` call would fail. Use `logger.debug(builder.toString())` (or `logger.debugf("%s", builder)`) so the message is logged verbatim.

findings.title: Indefinite-length handling in ASN1Decoder.readLength is inappropriate for DER
findings.body: The decoder returns `-1` for the BER indefinite-length form (length byte `0x80`). ECDSA signatures are required to be DER-encoded, where indefinite-length encoding is forbidden, so this branch is unreachable. More importantly, the value `-1` is then used in `readSequence()` as `while (length > 0) { ... length = length - bytes.length; }`, which is an infinite loop because `-1` is never `> 0` and `length - bytes.length` is always negative, so the loop body never executes and the method returns an empty list. While DER won't trigger this, the decoder is also fed other inputs (e.g. the inner INTEGER TLVs in `asn1derToConcatenatedRS`) and any caller that ever sends a BER-style indefinite-length value will get a silent zero-element list instead of an error. Either throw an IOException for indefinite length (DER requires definite length) or document and handle `-1` explicitly.
